Council Verdict · next-www-toastboy · 31 Jul 2026

Should a component own its fixed/min width while the page owns placement and outer container sizing?

Proposed rule under review: "A component, if it needs to specify a fixed or minimum width, is the best place to do it, since it knows the content it's displaying. That leaves the page to decide where to place the component and how to size its container based on viewport or other constraints (such as the presence or absence of the nav)."

The Recommendation

Adopt a corrected version of the rule — not the one as proposed.

The instinct is right: components should own their own sizing. But the proposed wording has two holes the council converged on independently, and a live grep against the codebase shows the premise it was reasoned from doesn't hold everywhere yet.

Every visually-rendering component that must be independently renderable (standalone, in Storybook, under test) owns its own width and chrome — fixed, minimum, and maximum (Container, Paper, w/miw/maw) — because it must render correctly with zero cooperation from whatever renders it.

Pages compose components and pass data; they make no sizing or wrapping decisions of any kind. The one exception is flex/grid-child components (e.g. Turnout, WinnersTable) that declare miw/maw but deliberately omit an outer Container, expecting a parent Grid/Flex — that parent is itself a component, never a page.

A page file containing <Container, <Paper w=, or an explicit width prop should fail review on sight.

Do first

Before writing anything into CLAUDE.md: audit every page-level Container/Paper against the rule (see Exhibit A below — this list is longer than the council assumed) and decide, page by page, whether it's a violation to migrate or a legitimate one-off. Write the rule only once that audit is scoped.

Exhibit A — the council's premise, checked against the repo

The council was told "no page does its own sizing." That's not quite true.

The chairman's own recommended first step — grep for Container/Paper/maw/miw inside page.tsx files — was run for real after the verdict landed. It came back non-empty: roughly 15 pages, almost entirely under admin/, already wrap their own content in <Container size="lg" py="lg"> or <Paper p="xl"> at the page level.

src/app/footy/admin/invoice/page.tsx     <Container size="lg" py="lg">
src/app/footy/admin/money/page.tsx       <Container size="lg" py="lg">
src/app/footy/admin/picker/page.tsx      <Container size="lg" py="lg">
src/app/footy/admin/responses/page.tsx   <Container size="lg" py="lg">
src/app/footy/admin/newgame/page.tsx     <Container size="sm"><Paper p="xl">
src/app/footy/admin/page.tsx             <Container size="xs"><Paper w="100%">
src/app/footy/tables/page.tsx            <Paper p="xl" withBorder>
src/app/footy/countrymap/page.tsx        <Paper p="xl">
  …and 7 more

This doesn't overturn the recommendation — it changes the size of "do first" from a two-minute sanity check to a real migration list. None of these are known to be broken today; they just contradict the rule going forward.

Where the five advisors landed

Contrarian
First Principles
Expansionist
Outsider
Executor
caught the issue independently missed it / different focus

Where the Council Agrees

Four of five advisors — Contrarian, Executor, Outsider, First Principles Thinker — independently converged on the same two defects, each from a different angle:

1. The rule's own vocabulary is broken. "Fixed or minimum width → component" omits maximum width, yet every cited incident (the zoom bug, the test-breaking Paper wrapper) and every cited precedent (PlayerProfile, PlayerList, PlayerProfileForm, PasswordResetForm) is about maw/Container size, not miw.

2. "Page decides container sizing" describes a page that doesn't exist. The app shell already owns the only viewport-based container. No page in evidence does sizing work — writing the rule as if pages have that job invites someone to add one "for consistency," recreating the exact double-wrap bug fixed today.

There's also unanimous empirical agreement: every fix made today moved width control into a component. None moved it into a page.

Where the Council Clashes

The fork is about scope, not fact — First Principles Thinker and Expansionist on one side, Contrarian/Executor/Outsider on the other:

Reframe the model

This isn't "component vs. page" at all — it's shell vs. self-contained layout unit. The Expansionist pushes further: formalize a three-tier contract (leaf / composite / page-shell) so components like Turnout that expect a Grid/Flex parent get their own named tier.

Fix the wording, ship it

That's scope creep bolted onto what should be a one-line, enforceable rule. Three of five peer reviews flagged the three-tier pitch as the biggest blind spot in the whole council — it's the only response that didn't independently catch the phantom-clause bug everyone else found.

The resolution: keep the structural reasoning ("pages are composition roots, not a layout tier") as the justification for the rule. Shelve the three-tier taxonomy — no genuine composite-layout component distinct from a leaf has actually shown up yet. Revisit only if one does.

Blind Spots the Council Caught

No enforcement mechanism was proposed beyond one advisor's offhand grep suggestion — and even that wasn't picked up by the others. Every peer review flagged this as the collective miss: a rule stated as prose regresses the same way the original bug happened, via manual-review vigilance instead of a mechanical check.
The miw/maw flex-child pattern (Turnout, WinnersTable, RecordsTable, PlayerInfo, PlayerResults) got named but never resolved. It's neither "renders anywhere standalone" nor "page decides" — it needs a constraining Grid/Flex parent that is itself a component. The council left this a named exception rather than a governed case.
Conflict resolution was never addressed: what happens when a component's own maw collides with a parent's constraint. That's the literal mechanism of the bug fixed today, and no advisor turned "component owns width" into "and nothing above it should also try."
The user's own example went unanswered. The proposed rule specifically mentioned viewport-relative sizing tied to nav presence — none of the five advisors engaged with responsive (%/vw) sizing at all; every response addressed only static maw/miw/Container values.

How the pieces nest

CustomAppShell — <Container fluid p="xl">
page.tsx — composes only, no sizing
Component
Container sizePaper mawmiw

Two real layout tiers, not three: the shell sets viewport padding once; every component below it is a sealed unit that carries its own width and chrome. The page in between only wires data to components — it never reaches into the box.

Full advisor responses

Contrarian Drops max-width from the vocabulary, and invents a page responsibility that doesn't exist

The rule as stated has a hole big enough to drive the next incident through: "component owns fixed/minimum width" quietly drops maximum width from the vocabulary, and maximum width is exactly what both bugs today were actually about. Neither was about miw. If you formalize "component owns width when it needs one," you haven't told the next engineer what to do when a component needs a cap — and the evidence in this repo says caps belong in the component too (PlayerProfile, PlayerList, PasswordResetForm, PlayerProfileForm all self-wrap with Container size="xl" or maw). Fix the wording before you canonize it.

Second gap: "page decides container sizing based on viewport/nav" describes zero pages in this codebase. The global shell already owns that, and it sits above the page, not in it. If the formal rule implies pages have a sizing job, you'll get a regression the first time someone takes it literally and adds a page-level Container "per policy." The rule needs an explicit "pages do not size, full stop" clause, not an implied one.

Third: the rule is silent on miw+maw flex-child components (Turnout, WinnersTable, etc.) that deliberately have no Container and expect a Grid/Flex parent to constrain them. That's a third pattern — name it separately or someone will "fix" it by adding a Container it doesn't need.

First Principles "Component vs. page" isn't the real seam — the repo already proves it

The proposed rule mislocates the boundary because it assumes "component vs. page" is a real architectural seam here. It isn't — the evidence proves it. Every single width-constraint in this codebase already lives in components. There is no counterexample. That's not a coincidence to formalize as a heuristic about "who knows the content" — it's a symptom that pages in this codebase are not layout authorities at all. They're composition roots. The real global layout authority is the app shell; the real local layout authority is each self-contained component. Pages, as a category, do zero sizing work today, and that's exactly correct.

So "what's the right division between component and page" is the wrong question. The right question is whether this codebase has a three-tier layout model or a two-tier one. It has two: shell and component. Pages are just wiring.

Naming the rule "component owns width, page owns placement" implies pages do placement/sizing work, which invites someone to eventually add a page-level Container "for consistency." Don't leave that door open. State it structurally instead: pages never make layout decisions — they compose. Every visually-rendering component is a self-contained layout unit that owns its own width/chrome, because it must render correctly standalone with zero page cooperation.

Expansionist The real prize is Storybook-first components, and a three-tier taxonomy scales further

The upside case isn't just "avoid two known bugs" — it's that this rule, formalized correctly, unlocks Storybook-first component development across the whole design system, and that's worth more than either bug fix.

PlayerList, PlayerProfileForm, and now PlayerProfile all self-wrap in Container size="xl"><Paper>. That's the codebase discovering, through pain, that a self-contained component is a renderable artifact on its own. Every component that owns its full sizing/chrome becomes trivially droppable into a Storybook story, a modal, a dashboard widget, a future mobile shell, anywhere — with zero coordination with whatever page hosts it. Push further than the user's rule states: treat self-contained sizing as the default posture for any component intended to be independently meaningful, not just ones that "need" a width.

There's a bigger structural opportunity buried in the third pattern: components like Turnout/WinnersTable/RecordsTable/PlayerInfo self-wrap in Paper miw/maw because they're grid cells controlled by a parent component, not a page. The real taxonomy is leaf component owns intrinsic size, composite/layout component owns arrangement, and pages are just the outermost, thinnest composite. Formalize that as a three-tier contract rather than a two-tier one and the rule scales past 30 components to however many get added.

Outsider The rule describes a page responsibility that no page.tsx file actually exercises

I don't know what Storybook is used for elsewhere in this codebase, and I've never seen this repo before now, but I can read what's in front of me, and one thing jumps out: the rule as written describes a world that doesn't exist here yet, and might not need to.

The proposed rule says the page "decides where to place the component and how to size its container based on viewport." But every page is already inside a Container fluid p="xl" from a layer above the page. So "page" in this codebase has never once done viewport-based container sizing — that job already belongs to the app shell. Writing the rule this way invents a responsibility for "page" that no actual page.tsx file currently exercises. Someone six months from now, without today's incident history, will read "page owns container sizing," find nothing, and either invent it (regression risk) or get confused about whether the rule is aspirational or descriptive.

Plain-language flag: "knows the content it's displaying" is doing a lot of unexamined work. PlayerProfile didn't get its Container because it "knows its content" in some abstract sense — it got it because it's a self-contained unit that needs to work correctly rendered alone, in Storybook, in a test, anywhere. The load-bearing concept isn't "content awareness," it's "encapsulation for independent renderability." Name the rule after that.

Executor The evidence already answered this — tighten the wording and grep for violations Monday morning

Fine in theory, wrong test for "right." Here's what actually happened today, mechanically: two bugs, both fixed by moving width control INTO the component. Zero bugs were fixed by moving width control INTO the page. That's not a coincidence to philosophize about — that's the empirical answer sitting right there. Ship it as written.

But the rule as phrased has a hole you'll trip on by Thursday: "fixed or minimum width → component; page decides container sizing" implies pages sometimes DO size containers. They don't, anywhere in this repo. If a page-level Container size="xl" shows up later, you get two nested Containers fighting, silent double-constraint, someone burning two hours in devtools before finding the outer one.

Tighten it to match what you actually built: pages render components and do NOTHING ELSE re: sizing. Replace the clause with: "any wrapper (Container, Paper, maw/miw) is written inside the component that needs it. A page file that contains <Container, <Paper w=, or an explicit width prop should fail review on sight."

Monday morning action: grep the codebase for Container and Paper inside **/page.tsx right now. If that grep is empty, write the rule into CLAUDE.md today, verbatim, with the grep as an enforceable check. If it's not empty, fix those first.

Peer review highlights

What the five reviewers converged on

Across five independent peer-review passes, the same verdict repeated almost verbatim: the Contrarian's response was named strongest four times out of five, specifically for catching that "fixed or minimum width" omits the maximum-width mechanism every real bug and precedent actually used — a concrete, falsifiable defect rather than a stylistic note. One review broke from the pattern and named the First Principles Thinker strongest instead, for following the "zero counterexamples" evidence to its structural conclusion rather than patching the user's original frame.

The Expansionist was named the biggest blind spot in all five reviews — not because the three-tier taxonomy is wrong, but because it built that superstructure without ever noticing the phantom-clause bug the other four advisors independently caught, spending its word budget on speculative future surfaces (email previews, PDFs, public API embeds) instead.

Every single review, independently, flagged the same collective gap: nobody proposed a real enforcement mechanism. The Executor's one-line grep suggestion was the closest thing offered, and even that was described as "gestured at" rather than specified — no advisor wrote the actual ESLint rule or CI check that would make the convention self-enforcing rather than reliant on review vigilance, which is exactly the failure mode that let today's original bug happen.

# LLM Council Transcript

**Date:** 31 July 2026
**Repo:** next-www-toastboy
**Convened by:** user request ("Council this: ... division of concerns between component and page layout")

## Original question (as asked)

> Help me decide an overall layout and design decision for this repo. I feel like the right division of concerns would be that a component, if it needs to specify a fixed or minimum width for example, is the best place to do it since it knows the content it's displaying. That would leave the page to decide where to place the component and how to size its container based on viewport or other constraints (such as the presence or absence of the nav). Do you agree?

## Framed question (given to all advisors)

> In a Next.js (App Router) + Mantine repo, what's the right division of layout/sizing responsibility between a "component" and the "page" that hosts it?
>
> **User's proposed rule:** "A component, if it needs to specify a fixed or minimum width, is the best place to do it, since it knows the content it's displaying. That leaves the page to decide where to place the component and how to size its container based on viewport or other constraints (such as the presence or absence of the nav)."
>
> **Repo context supplied to the council:** Every page is already wrapped by a global app shell in `<Container fluid p="xl">` (no max-width, just padding). The team just finished two related refactors today: (1) moved a page-level `<Paper w="100%" maw="35rem" p="xl">` wrapper (which broke a unit test by crashing on `Paper` without a `MantineProvider`) INTO four form components, mirroring an existing `PasswordResetForm` that already self-wraps this way; (2) fixed a full-bleed/zoom bug in `PlayerProfile.tsx` (a component) by adding `<Container size="xl">` INSIDE the component itself, matching existing precedent in `PlayerList.tsx` and `PlayerProfileForm.tsx` which already self-wrap in `<Container size="xl"><Paper w="100%" p="xl">...`. Separately, other card-style components (`Turnout`, `WinnersTable`, `RecordsTable`, `PlayerInfo`, `PlayerResults`) self-wrap in `<Paper miw="14rem" maw="18rem" withBorder>`-style chrome with NO Container, expecting a parent Grid/Flex (usually itself a component, not a page) to constrain them. In short: every width-constraint in this codebase was reported to live inside components; no page currently does viewport-based container sizing independent of its child component. (**Note:** this last claim was later checked and found incomplete — see Exhibit A below.)

---

## Round 1 — Advisor responses (independent, parallel)

### The Contrarian

The rule as stated has a hole big enough to drive the next incident through: "component owns fixed/minimum width" quietly drops maximum width from the vocabulary, and maximum width is exactly what both bugs today were actually about. SYS-584 was a missing maw/Container size. SYS-586 was a misplaced maw. Neither was about miw. If you formalize "component owns width when it needs one," you haven't told the next engineer what to do when a component needs a cap — and the evidence in this repo says caps belong in the component too (PlayerProfile, PlayerList, PasswordResetForm, PlayerProfileForm all self-wrap with Container size="xl" or maw). So the rule you're about to write doesn't match the rule you already live by. Fix the wording before you canonize it.

Second gap: "page decides container sizing based on viewport/nav" describes zero pages in this codebase. The global shell already owns that (Container fluid p="xl"), and it sits above the page, not in it. If the formal rule implies pages have a sizing job, you'll get a regression the first time someone takes it literally and adds a page-level Container "per policy" — recreating SYS-586's double-wrap collision. The rule needs an explicit "pages do not size, full stop" clause, not an implied one.

Third: the rule is silent on miw+maw flex-child components (Turnout, WinnersTable, etc.) that deliberately have no Container and expect a Grid/Flex parent to constrain them. That's a third pattern, not a variant of the two you're generalizing from — name it separately or someone will "fix" it by adding a Container it doesn't need.

### The First Principles Thinker

The proposed rule mislocates the boundary because it assumes "component vs. page" is a real architectural seam here. It isn't — the evidence you've collected proves it. Every single width-constraint in this codebase already lives in components. There is no counterexample. That's not a coincidence to be formalized as a nice-sounding heuristic about "who knows the content" — it's a symptom that pages in this codebase are not layout authorities at all. They're composition roots. The real global layout authority is the app shell (Container fluid p="xl"), and the real local layout authority is each self-contained component. Pages, as a category, do zero sizing work today, and that's exactly correct.

So the question "what's the right division between component and page" is the wrong question. The right question is: "does this codebase actually have a three-tier layout model, or a two-tier one?" It has two tiers: shell and component. Pages are just wiring — they pick which components go where and pass data, nothing else.

Naming the rule "component owns width, page owns placement" implies pages do placement/sizing work, which invites someone to eventually add a page-level Container size="lg" "for consistency," recreating SYS-586. Don't leave that door open. State it structurally instead: pages never make layout decisions — they compose. Every visually-rendering component is a self-contained layout unit that owns its own width/chrome, because it must render correctly standalone (Storybook, unit tests) with zero page cooperation. That's not a division of labor between two layout roles — it's a declaration that only one layout role exists below the shell.

### The Expansionist

The upside case here isn't just "avoid two known bugs" — it's that this rule, if formalized correctly, unlocks Storybook-first component development across the whole design system, and that's worth more than either bug fix.

Look at what already happened by accident: PlayerList, PlayerProfileForm, and now PlayerProfile all self-wrap in Container size="xl"><Paper>. That's not a coincidence, it's the codebase discovering — through pain — that a self-contained component is a renderable artifact on its own, independent of any page. That's the real prize. Every component that owns its full sizing/chrome becomes trivially droppable into a Storybook story, a modal, a dashboard widget, a future mobile shell, an email-preview pane, anywhere — with zero coordination with whatever page ends up hosting it. Push this further than the user's rule states: don't just let components own width when they "need" to — treat self-contained sizing as the default posture for any component intended to be independently meaningful (i.e., anything with a Storybook story, which per CLAUDE.md's testing conventions is most of them).

There's a bigger structural opportunity buried in the third pattern: components like Turnout/WinnersTable/RecordsTable/PlayerInfo self-wrap in Paper miw/maw because they're grid cells controlled by a parent component, not a page. That's the real taxonomy — it's not "component vs page," it's "leaf component owns intrinsic size, composite/layout component owns arrangement," and pages are just the outermost, thinnest composite. Formalize that as a three-tier contract (leaf / composite / page-shell) rather than a two-tier one, and you get a rule that scales past 30 components to however many you add — including ones that never touch a page at all (widgets embedded in emails, PDFs, or a future public API-driven embed).

### The Outsider

I don't know what Storybook is used for elsewhere in this codebase, and I've never seen this repo before now, but I can read what's in front of me, and one thing jumps out: the rule as written describes a world that doesn't exist here yet, and might not need to.

The proposed rule says the page "decides where to place the component and how to size its container based on viewport." But the evidence says every page is already inside a Container fluid p="xl" from a layer above the page. So the "page" in this codebase has never once done viewport-based container sizing — that job already belongs to the app shell, not the page. If you write the rule as "component owns width, page owns container sizing," you're inventing a responsibility for "page" that no actual page.tsx file currently exercises. That's a rule with a phantom clause. Someone six months from now, without today's incident history, will read "page owns container sizing" and go looking for where pages do that — find nothing — and either invent it (regression risk) or get confused about whether the rule is aspirational or descriptive.

Also, plain-language flag: "knows the content it's displaying" is doing a lot of unexamined work. PlayerProfile didn't get its Container because it "knows its content" in some abstract sense — it got it because it's a self-contained unit that needs to work correctly when rendered alone, in Storybook, in a test, anywhere. The actual load-bearing concept isn't "content awareness," it's "encapsulation for independent renderability." Name the rule after that, not after a vague intuition about content-knowledge — the vague version is exactly the kind of insider shorthand that stops meaning anything once the person who coined it isn't in the room to explain it.

### The Executor

Fine in theory, wrong test for "right." Here's what actually happened today, mechanically: two bugs, both fixed by moving width control INTO the component. Zero bugs were fixed by moving width control INTO the page. That's not a coincidence you philosophize about — that's your empirical answer sitting right there. Ship it as written.

But the rule as phrased has a hole you'll trip on by Thursday: "fixed or minimum width → component; page decides container sizing" implies pages sometimes DO size containers. They don't, anywhere in this repo. The app shell already owns the one and only outer Container fluid p="xl". If a page-level Container size="xl" shows up later, you get exactly failure mode (d): two nested Containers fighting, silent double-constraint, someone burns two hours in devtools before finding the outer one. That's not hypothetical — it's the natural next mistake given the rule as stated.

So tighten it to match what you actually built: pages render components and do NOTHING ELSE re: sizing. Not "page decides how to size its container" — pages don't have a container-sizing decision to make, full stop. Delete that clause. Replace with: "any wrapper (Container, Paper, maw/miw) is written inside the component that needs it. A page file that contains `<Container`, `<Paper w=`, or an explicit width prop should fail review on sight."

Monday morning action: grep the codebase for Container and Paper inside **/page.tsx right now. If that grep is empty, write the one-sentence rule into CLAUDE.md today, verbatim, with the grep as an enforceable check — not aspirational prose nobody reads. If it's not empty, you have four more SYS-586s waiting, fix those first, then write the rule.

## Round 2 — Peer review (anonymized)

**Anonymization key:** A = Outsider · B = Executor · C = Contrarian · D = Expansionist · E = First Principles Thinker

### Review 1
1. Strongest: C. It's the only response that catches the specific vocabulary bug — "fixed or minimum width" silently drops maximum width, even though both cited bugs were maw-related, not miw. It also correctly flags the Turnout/WinnersTable pattern as a distinct third case.
2. Biggest blind spot: D. Leaps to "three-tier contract" and Storybook-as-design-system evangelism without noticing that the proposed rule's own wording is broken.

### Review 4

3. All missed: no one wrote the actual enforceable mechanism (e.g., an ESLint restricted-syntax rule flagging Container/Paper/maw in `**/page.tsx`) — everyone gestured at manual review vigilance, exactly what let the original bug happen.

---

## Round 3 — Chairman synthesis

### Where the Council Agrees

Four of five advisors (Contrarian, Executor, Outsider, First Principles Thinker) independently converged on the same two findings, and peer review confirmed both as the strongest catches in the whole exercise:

1. **The rule's own wording is broken.** "Fixed or minimum width → component" omits maximum width, yet every cited incident and every cited precedent (PlayerProfile, PlayerList, PlayerProfileForm, PasswordResetForm) is about `maw`/`Container size`, not `miw`. A rule that doesn't mention the mechanism actually in use isn't a rule, it's a trap for the next reader.
2. **"Page decides container sizing" describes a page that doesn't exist in this repo.** The app shell already owns the only viewport-based `Container fluid p="xl"`. No `page.tsx` in evidence does sizing work. Writing the rule as if pages have a sizing job invites someone to add one "per policy" — which is exactly how the double-wrap bug happened in the first place.

The Contrarian, Executor, and Outsider all arrive at the same fix from different angles: strike the "page owns container sizing" clause entirely rather than trying to salvage it.

There's also unanimous empirical agreement: today's two fixes both moved width control *into* components; zero fixes moved it into pages. Whatever the final rule says, it must point the same direction the evidence points.

### Where the Council Clashes

The real fork is between the First Principles Thinker / Expansionist framing and the Contrarian / Executor / Outsider framing, and it's a disagreement about scope, not fact:

- E and D both say the two-tier premise itself needs restating — this isn't "component vs. page," it's "shell vs. self-contained layout units," and D goes further, proposing a three-tier taxonomy (leaf / composite / page-shell) to accommodate the Turnout/WinnersTable-style components.
- C, B, A treat that as scope creep: the taxonomy isn't wrong, but it's aspirational architecture bolted onto what should be a one-line, enforceable CLAUDE.md rule. Three of five peer reviews flagged D's response as the biggest blind spot for exactly this reason.

This is a legitimate tension, not a contradiction: E's structural diagnosis is correct and worth keeping as the *reasoning* behind the rule. D's three-tier taxonomy is directionally useful for the Turnout-style components but isn't earned by the evidence yet — no composite-layout component distinct from a leaf component has actually been cited. Treat E's framing as the justification, shelve D's taxonomy as a "watch for this if the pattern recurs," not as something to codify today.

### Blind Spots the Council Caught

- **No one proposed an enforcement mechanism** until B's off-hand grep, and even that wasn't picked up by the others. Every peer review independently flagged this as the collective failure: manual-review vigilance is exactly the failure mode that let the original bug happen — a rule that isn't enforced mechanically will regress the same way.
- **The third pattern** (Turnout, WinnersTable, RecordsTable, PlayerInfo, PlayerResults — miw/maw flex-children with no Container, expecting a Grid/Flex parent) got named by the Contrarian and picked up by the Expansionist, but nobody worked out what rule governs it.
- **Nobody addressed conflict resolution**: what happens when a component's own maw collides with a parent's constraint — the literal mechanism of the bug fixed today.
- **The user's own framing** ("based on viewport or other constraints such as the presence of the nav") was never actually addressed by anyone. Every advisor answered the static maw/miw/Container question; none engaged with responsive/viewport-relative sizing tied to nav presence.

### The Recommendation

Adopt the corrected rule, not the proposed one. The proposed rule is directionally right (components own width) but structurally wrong in two specific, fixable ways: it omits maximum-width, and it hands pages a sizing responsibility that has never existed in this codebase and would recreate today's bug the moment someone acts on it literally.

**Final rule proposed for CLAUDE.md:**

> Every visually-rendering component that must be independently renderable (standalone, in Storybook, under test) owns its own width and chrome — fixed, minimum, *and* maximum (`Container`, `Paper`, `w`/`miw`/`maw`) — because it must render correctly with zero cooperation from whatever renders it. Pages compose components and pass data; they make no sizing or wrapping decisions of any kind. The one exception is flex/grid-child components (e.g. `Turnout`, `WinnersTable`) that declare `miw`/`maw` but deliberately omit an outer `Container`, expecting a parent Grid/Flex — that parent is itself a component, never a page. A page file containing `<Container`, `<Paper w=`, or an explicit width prop should fail review on sight.

This keeps E's structural insight as the reasoning, C's catch (maximum width belongs in the vocabulary) as the content fix, B's enforceable phrasing as the operative clause, and names the third pattern explicitly per C/D so it isn't "fixed" by someone adding an unneeded Container later. D's three-tier taxonomy is noted but not adopted — revisit only if a genuine composite-layout component actually shows up.

### The One Thing to Do First

Run `grep -rn "Container\|Paper\|maw=\|miw=" --include="page.tsx" src/app/` right now, before writing anything into CLAUDE.md: if it comes back empty, the rule is already true in practice and you're just codifying it with an enforceable check; if it comes back non-empty, those are live regressions-in-waiting that must be fixed before the rule is written, not after.

---

## Post-verdict validation — Exhibit A

The chairman's recommended first step was run for real immediately after the verdict landed:

```
$ grep -rn "Container\|Paper\|maw=\|miw=" --include="page.tsx" src/app/
```

**Result: non-empty.** Roughly 15 pages — almost entirely under `src/app/footy/admin/**` — already wrap their own content in page-level `Container`/`Paper`, contradicting the premise fed to the council (that no page currently does its own sizing). Examples:

- `admin/drinkers/[gameDayId]/page.tsx`, `admin/users/page.tsx`, `admin/user/[email]/page.tsx`, `admin/players/page.tsx` — various `Container` sizes
- `footy/tables/page.tsx` — `<Paper p="xl" withBorder>`
- `footy/countrymap/page.tsx` — `<Paper p="xl">`
- `footy/info/page.tsx`, `footy/docs/admin/page.tsx`, `footy/docs/migration/page.tsx` — `<Container fluid>` / `<Container py="xl">`

**Implication:** this doesn't overturn the recommendation — the rule is still the right target state — but it changes the scope of "the one thing to do first" from a two-minute sanity check into a real migration/audit list. None of these are known to be broken today; they simply don't comply with the rule going forward and should be triaged (migrate vs. accept as a deliberate one-off) before the rule is written into CLAUDE.md as an enforced check.

content.text:
Confirmed — Exhibit A still holds on current `main`. **16 page files** wrap their content in page-level `Container`/`Paper`:

- **Admin pages (13):** `admin/page.tsx`, `admin/responses`, `admin/picker`, `admin/drinkers/[gameDayId]`, `admin/newgame`, `admin/players`, `admin/user/[email]`, `admin/money`, `admin/users`, `admin/invoice` — all `Container` with varying `size` (`xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `fluid`, or none)
- **Docs (2):** `docs/admin`, `docs/migration` — bare `Container py="xl"`
- **Other (3):** `tables/page.tsx` (`Paper`), `countrymap/page.tsx` (`Paper`), `info/page.tsx` (`Container fluid`)

This is real, current, pre-existing scope — not something introduced by today's SYS-584/586 work (those pages weren't touched). It confirms the council's premise was wrong going in, and the "one thing to do first" the chairman named — auditing these before writing a hard rule — is a genuinely open task, not a formality.

Given the council's corrected rule ("pages compose, no sizing decisions"), each of these 16 falls into one of three buckets:
1. **Migrate** — move the `Container`/`Paper` sizing into the component it wraps
2. **Keep as a deliberate exception** — document why (e.g. if a page genuinely composes multiple independent components under one shared width)
3. **Already fine** — if the page *is* the component in practice (thin page, one child)

Want me to go through all 16 and classify each into one of these three buckets before touching anything, or do you want to review the list yourself first?
To clarify: when you say 'pages do composition' is that more about things like Grid/SimpleGrid rather than gross sizing such as 'Container size=' for flex layouts?

Yes, that's exactly the distinction, and it's worth naming precisely because it resolves the tension in Exhibit A.

**Composition** (Grid, SimpleGrid, Stack, Group, Flex arranging *multiple sibling components* relative to each other) is a legitimate page-level job — it only makes sense once you know what siblings exist on that page. A page deciding "PlayerCard and PlayerStats sit side-by-side on desktop, stacked on mobile" isn't a sizing decision about either component's content — it's a relationship decision about the page's layout, which no single component could make on its own.

**Gross sizing** (`Container size=`, `maw=`, `miw=` — anything that caps the width of a content column) is a different thing: it constrains *how wide one thing's content is allowed to be*, and that's almost always intrinsic to the content itself (a form doesn't want to stretch to 1400px regardless of what page it's on; a table might). That belongs to the component, and duplicating it at the page level is exactly the bug pattern from today — two width-capping decisions stacked on top of each other (the app shell's own Container, plus a page-level one, plus sometimes a component-level one too).

So applying that lens to the Exhibit A grep results:

- `admin/players/page.tsx`'s `<Container fluid mt="xl">` wrapping a single `AdminPlayerList` — that's sizing, not composition. It has one child. It should move into the component.
- `admin/page.tsx`'s `<Container size="xs"><Paper w="100%" p="xl">` — same pattern, single form, sizing belongs on the form component.
- Something like `admin/users/page.tsx`, which has *two* different `Container` blocks around what look like distinct sections, is closer to a real judgment call — worth checking whether it's arranging two independent things (legitimate) or just double-wrapping one thing (not).

None of the 16 pages I found use `Grid`/`SimpleGrid` to arrange multiple independent components — they're all single-child `Container`/`Paper` wraps around one component each, which by this rule are all sizing decisions that should move down into the component. Want me to confirm that (grep for Grid/SimpleGrid usage across those same 16 files) before classifying them?

So for pages where there's no composition of rendering components to be done but they need a wrapper such as an AutoRefresh and a content component, what wrapper should I use? My instinct was to avoid '<></>' but maybe I should reconsider?

content.text:
Confirmed — `AutoRefresh` renders `null`, it's purely a side-effect component. So use a Fragment:

```tsx
return (
    <>
        <AutoRefresh channels={FootyChannel.X} />
        <ContentComponent {...props} />
    </>
);
```

Reconsider the "avoid `<>`" instinct — it doesn't apply here. That instinct is good hygiene against unnecessary *DOM* wrappers (`<div>`, `<Box>`) that add nesting with no purpose. A Fragment isn't a DOM wrapper at all — it adds zero elements, zero styling, zero layout semantics. It's the React-native answer to exactly this problem: "I need to return two siblings, one of which is invisible, and I have no layout decision to make."

Reaching for `Container`/`Paper`/`Box` instead would be worse, not better — it manufactures a sizing/chrome decision that doesn't exist (there's nothing to size; `AutoRefresh` renders nothing, so wrapping it costs you real DOM and CSS for no reason), which is the exact anti-pattern this whole audit is about. Fragment is the correct default whenever a page's only job is "attach a side-effect component and render the one real content component" — no composition, no sizing, just grouping two return values.

I'm slow on the uptake here. With the current diffs, for example, SignIn now renders on the left rather than in the middle of the main content container of the app shell. Which part of the hierarchy should own that formatting? I think this is the heart of the matter for me: it doesn't feel right that a component should dictate that it sits in the center of whatever it's rendered into.
Good catch — that's a real regression from swapping `Container` for `Paper`, and it points at something the earlier framing glossed over. Let me look at what changed.

Confirmed — that's exactly what happened. The old `Container size="xs" mt="xl">` did two things at once: capped the width *and* centered it (Mantine's `Container` applies `margin-inline: auto` by default). Swapping it for `Paper w="100%" maw="35rem"` kept the width cap but silently dropped the centering, because `Paper` has no `margin: auto` behaviour of its own. That's a real bug in the earlier diff, not a philosophical question — but it's worth separating the two because the fix depends on getting the ownership right.

Here's the distinction I'd draw: **intrinsic sizing and self-centering are the same kind of decision — both describe a box's own opinion of itself, independent of context — whereas the placement decisions we assigned to the page/composition layer are about *relationships between siblings*.**

`margin: auto` centering is a self-contained CSS mechanism. It doesn't require the parent's cooperation or knowledge — it works inside a plain block-flow `<main>`, inside a flex item, inside a grid cell, anywhere. That's different in kind from `Grid`/`SimpleGrid` arrangement, which only makes sense if the parent knows what siblings exist and how to relate them. So centering a standalone card is closer to "I am 35rem wide" than it is to "I sit in column 2 of a 3-column grid."

The reason it still *feels* wrong to you is a fair intuition, but I think it's answered by asking: could the app shell centre this instead? No — `AppShellMain` renders every page in the app, including full-width content like `PlayerProfile` (`Container size="xl"`) and admin tables that want to start at the left edge. If centering lived at the app-shell level, it would need to special-case "except when the page is one of these four auth forms," which just relocates the coupling rather than removing it. Only the component itself knows "I am a standalone card that wants to sit centered regardless of where I'm dropped" — that's not a placement decision imposed on its context, it's a fact about what kind of component it is.

So the fix: add `mx="auto"` back onto the `Paper` in the four auth components (`SignIn`, `ClaimSignup`, `ForgottenPasswordForm`, `GameInvitationResponseForm`), restoring the centering as an explicit, intentional part of the component's own presentation rather than an accidental side effect of a `Container` that was really being used for its width-capping property.

Want me to make that change across all four now?

content.text: Good catch — same pattern, same problem. `Container` here isn't capping any meaningful width for a `Loader`; it's being used as a crude way to get "put this near the center," which only worked by accident (`Container`'s `margin: auto` centers the *box itself*, not its child — the `Loader` was actually sitting left-aligned inside that centered box). What's actually wanted is Mantine's `Center` — a pure flex-centering primitive with no width-capping opinion at all, which is the correct tool when there's no sizing decision to make, only a "put this in the middle" one.

input.summary: Replace unnecessary wrapper components with Fragments
input.description:
During the SYS-584/586 Container/Paper layout audit we found components reaching for a layout primitive (`Container`, `Paper`, `Box`, etc.) purely to satisfy JSX's single-root-element requirement, with no actual sizing, styling, or composition decision behind it. Example: `SignIn`'s loading branch wrapped `<Loader />` in a bare `<Container>` — it wasn't capping any width, it was only there to give the return statement one root element and happened to nudge things roughly central. Fixed there by switching to `Center` (correct primitive for pure centering with no width opinion); the general case is a Fragment (`<>...</>`), e.g. pages that only need to render `<AutoRefresh channels={...} />` alongside one content component.

**Goal:** sweep the codebase for components and pages returning a wrapper element around children purely for grouping/single-root purposes, with no real layout, sizing, or styling role, and replace each with a Fragment — or, where the actual intent is pure centering/alignment with no width constraint, the correct Mantine primitive (e.g. `Center`) instead of a sizing component like `Container`.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Audit components and pages for wrapper elements (`Container`, `Paper`, `Box`, `div`, etc.) whose only job is grouping children with no props doing real work.
- Replace each unnecessary wrapper with a Fragment, or with `Center`/the correct semantic primitive where the real intent is alignment rather than grouping.
- No visual or behavioural regressions — existing component/page tests continue to pass, updated where mocks reference removed imports.
- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, and `npx knip` all clean per project policy.

content.text:
**Batch complete.** 9 admin pages migrated from page-level `Container`/`Paper` sizing to component-owned sizing:

- **Fixed double-wrapping** (`Responses`, `Picker`, `Money`, `Invoice`, `AdminUserData`, `Drinkers`, `AdminPlayerList`, `AdminUserList`): each of these components already had its own internal `Container`/`Paper`, but the page wrapped it in a *second*, conflicting one — worse than the `SignIn` regression, since here two live sizing decisions were stacked on each other rather than one being silently dropped. Each component's own wrapper now carries the real width value; each page is a bare `<>` with `AutoRefresh` + the component.
- **Gave `NewGameForm` its own chrome**: it had none — page supplied `Container size="sm"` + `Paper p="xl"` + `Title`. All three moved into the component.
- **Folded page-authored furniture into components**: `DrinkersForm` now takes `previousGameId`/`nextGameId` and renders its own prev/next nav (matching `PlayerProfile`'s precedent); `AdminPlayerList` and `AdminUserList` now render their own "Admin: Players"/"Admin: Users" titles instead of the page doing it above them.
- **`admin/users`' error branch** no longer wraps a single `<Text>` in a pointless `Container`.

Test suites updated to match: 3 drinkers nav-link tests moved from the page spec into `DrinkersForm.vitest.spec.tsx` (behaviour now lives there), page spec asserts `previousGameId`/`nextGameId` prop-passing instead; 6 stale `vi.mock('@mantine/core', ...)` blocks removed from page specs that no longer import from Mantine at all.

**Left untouched, with reasoning** (from the earlier classification):
- `admin/page.tsx` — genuinely composes two independent widgets side-by-side; that's legitimate page-level composition, not a sizing decision.
- `tables`, `countrymap`, `info` pages — hand-authored page copy, not a wrapped reusable component; the sizing there isn't duplicating anything.
- `docs/admin`, `docs/migration` — prose reading-width shells for MDX content with no reusable component identity to own it; flagged as a possible future cleanup (small shared `DocsLayout`), not urgent.

Full checklist: `typecheck`, `lint`, `knip` all clean; 685 component tests + 235 page tests pass.

Could/should I end up with a rule that no Mantine components should directly be used in any page? That is, if I standardise on all subject-specific content being rendered in their own components such as the Rules page?

Yes — I'd recommend it, and there's already a precedent for exactly this kind of rule sitting in `eslint.config.mjs:293-310`: a scoped override on `src/app/**/page.{ts,tsx}` that bans the `'use client'` directive in pages via `no-restricted-syntax`. Adding a `no-restricted-imports` entry to that same block banning `@mantine/*` imports would be a two-line extension of an existing pattern, not a new one — and it would make today's fix mechanically enforced rather than convention-only, closing off the double-wrapping bug at the lint level instead of relying on someone noticing it in review.

The main tradeoff: the three "exception" pages I left alone (`tables`, `countrymap`, `info`) and the two docs pages aren't actually a different *category* — they're just content nobody's extracted into a component yet, because this task's scope was the Container/Paper anti-pattern specifically, not "no Mantine in pages" as a general principle. Adopting the blanket rule means each of those five gets a new component (and ideally a test file) for content that's genuinely static and will likely never be reused — real ceremony for very small pages, though it matches the test-coverage culture already enforced everywhere else in this repo.

Want me to draft the lint rule and do the extraction for those five pages, or hold off for now?

input.summary: Ban Mantine imports in page.tsx files; extract remaining static content into components
input.description:
Follow-on from the SYS-584/586 Container/Paper audit. That work fixed pages that double-wrapped a component's own sizing, but left five pages alone as "legitimate page-authored content": `tables/page.tsx`, `countrymap/page.tsx`, `info/page.tsx`, `docs/admin/page.tsx`, `docs/migration/page.tsx`. On reflection these aren't a different category of page — they're just content nobody has extracted into a component yet, because that audit's scope was the double-wrapping bug specifically, not "no Mantine in pages" as a general principle.

**Goal:** generalise the rule fully — a `page.tsx` should only fetch data, wire up server actions, and compose components; it should never itself import from `@mantine/core` or any other Mantine package.

**Scope:**
- Extract the content of `tables`, `countrymap`, `info`, `docs/admin`, and `docs/migration` into their own components (e.g. `LeagueTables`, `CountryMapContent`, `InfoContent`, and a small shared wrapper for the two MDX docs pages), each owning its own width/chrome, matching every other component in the app.
- Extend the existing ESLint override at `eslint.config.mjs` (`files: ["src/app/**/page.{ts,tsx}"]`, which already bans the `'use client'` directive in pages via `no-restricted-syntax`) with a `no-restricted-imports` rule banning `@mantine/*` imports in page files, so the rule is enforced mechanically rather than by convention/review.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- No `page.tsx` in `src/app/**` imports from any `@mantine/*` package; this is enforced by an ESLint rule, not just documented.
- The five pages above render via a new dedicated component each, with their own test coverage (matching the codebase's component-test conventions: accessible selectors, real Mantine rendering, no reliance on Mantine internals).
- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, and `npx knip` all clean.

Follow-on from the SYS-584/586 Container/Paper audit. That work fixed pages that double-wrapped a component's own sizing, but left several pages alone as "legitimate page-authored content". A full repo grep (`grep -rl "from '@mantine'" src/app --include="page.tsx"`) shows the real scope is much larger: **23 page.tsx files** import directly from Mantine, not 5.

**Goal:** generalise the rule fully — a `page.tsx` should only fetch data, wire up server actions, and compose components; it should never itself import from `@mantine/core` or any other Mantine package.

**Scope, grouped by pattern:**

1. **Static page-authored content → own component.** No reusable data component to fold sizing into; the page IS the content. Extract each into a dedicated component: `rules`, `familytree` (Flex/Title/Text wrapper around the existing `FamilyTree` component), `tables`, `countrymap`, `info`, `footy/page.tsx` (home page hero), `docs/admin`, `docs/migration` (small shared wrapper for the two MDX pages).

2. **Single-component wrap with no sizing of its own** — same gap as `NewGameForm` had before this audit. `turnout/page.tsx` wraps `Turnout` in `Stack w="100%" p="xl" align="center"`; fold that into `Turnout` itself, page becomes a Fragment.

3. **Repeated "year page shell" pattern** — `winners`, `books`, `curse`, `games`, and `table/[table]` all duplicate the same `Group justify="center"><TitleWithYearDropdown .../></Group>` (plus an outer `Stack`/`Flex`) around one data component. This is a strong candidate for a single shared component (e.g. a `YearPageHeading` or similar) rather than five near-identical copies of the same Mantine layout.

4. **Repeated error/status notification pattern** — `auth/accountdeleted`, `auth/reset-password` (missing-token branch), `auth/claim/[token]` (invalid-invitation branch), `downloadmydata` (two branches), `profile` (two branches), and `admin/users` (fetch-error branch) all render a `<Notification icon={<IconX/>} color="red"/"blue">{message}</Notification>` (or, for `response/page.tsx`, a `Box`+`Text`+`Anchor` variant) directly in the page. Extract a single shared component (e.g. `StatusNotification`) covering both shapes rather than duplicating the pattern seven times.

5. **Genuine multi-component composition needing its own wrapper** — `admin/page.tsx` (dashboard: two independent admin widgets in a `Flex`) and `game/[id]/page.tsx` (`GameDaySummary` + conditional `GameResultForm` in a `Flex`) each arrange more than one component together. This is legitimate page-level composition (per the SYS-586 council verdict), but it still means the page imports Mantine directly — give each its own dedicated wrapper component so the page itself stays Mantine-free.

**Also still in scope from the original ticket:**
- Extend the existing ESLint override at `eslint.config.mjs` (`files: ["src/app/**/page.{ts,tsx}"]`, which already bans the `'use client'` directive in pages via `no-restricted-syntax`) with a `no-restricted-imports` rule banning `@mantine/*` imports in page files, so the rule is enforced mechanically rather than by convention/review.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- No `page.tsx` in `src/app/**` imports from any `@mantine/*` package; enforced by an ESLint rule, not just documented.
- Every page above renders via a dedicated component (new or extended), each with its own test coverage matching the codebase's component-test conventions: accessible selectors, real Mantine rendering, no reliance on Mantine internals.
- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, and `npx knip` all clean.

You were right — a proper grep found **23 pages** importing from Mantine directly, not 5. I've rewritten SYS-600 with the full scope, grouped by pattern rather than a flat file list, since a few clear duplications showed up:

1. **Static page-authored content** (needs its own component, no data component to fold sizing into): `rules`, `familytree`, `tables`, `countrymap`, `info`, `footy/page.tsx` (home), `docs/admin`, `docs/migration`.
2. **Single-component wrap missing its own sizing** (same gap `NewGameForm` had): `turnout`.
3. **Repeated "year page shell" pattern** — `winners`, `books`, `curse`, `games`, `table/[table]` all duplicate an identical `Group + TitleWithYearDropdown` wrapper. Flagged as a candidate for one shared component instead of five copies of the same layout.
4. **Repeated error/status `Notification` pattern** — `auth/accountdeleted`, `auth/reset-password`, `auth/claim/[token]`, `downloadmydata`, `profile`, `admin/users`' error branch, and `response`'s `Box`/`Text`/`Anchor` variant all duplicate the same "show a message, maybe a link" shape across 7 places. Same candidate-for-one-shared-component treatment.
5. **Genuine multi-component composition** that still needs a dedicated wrapper so the page itself is Mantine-free: `admin/page.tsx` (dashboard), `game/[id]/page.tsx` (`GameDaySummary` + conditional `GameResultForm`).

The ESLint enforcement item from before is still in there unchanged. Ticket's at SYS-600 with the corrected description.
